t: Three Daylamite brothers took Fars, the Jibal and Iraq between 934 and 945 and ruled them as a family confederation.
Shia themselves, they kept the Sunni Abbasid caliphs as figureheads in Baghdad for 110 years.
Under Adud al-Dawla (d. 983) they reached their height; family rivalry then left them prey to the Ghaznavids and Seljuks.
dyk: The astronomer Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi dedicated his Book of Fixed Stars to Adud al-Dawla; it contains one of the earliest recorded descriptions of the Andromeda Galaxy.
ev: Ali ibn Buya takes Fars and makes Shiraz his base
Ahmad ibn Buya enters Baghdad and the brothers receive their titles
Public Ashura mourning and the feast of Ghadir are introduced in Baghdad
Adud al-Dawla defeats Bakhtiyar and unites the Buyid lands
Death of Adud al-Dawla, followed by rivalry among his sons
Tughril Beg enters Baghdad and ends Buyid rule in Iraq
The last Buyid prince in Fars is killed by Fadluya

f.founder: Imad al-Dawla (Ali ibn Buya) and his brothers
